pass_rule: pass only if every checker test is true: exact 36-cell matrix, terminal experiment, all 36 final attempts complete and accounted, all 36 cells complete and accounted on the first attempt (no rerun), every attempt within 100,000 tokens, reruns within the declared policy, six aggregate defect-case cells with non-empty mechanically valid v2 evidence, six assessed defect-case cells whose assessor actually ran (usage > 0) and completed with accounting
reference_profile: the gpt-6.1-sol profile that passed schedule r1 (2026-10-13-qualification-rerun) and draws r2, r3 (2026-10-13-tools-reliability-separating): batched context-read prompt (the only persona_inputs.py change from 2f1e95c to c8059bb appends citation_bound_prompt, which returns an empty string unless context.line_counts is on), 100,000 total ceiling, default assessor reservation (no --assessment-tokens; 20,000), same three pilot development cases, four focused arms, three repetitions, concurrency 3, six native turns, context enabled with the same related paths, rounds.max 3
unchanged_from_reference: context enabled with the same related paths; context.line_counts not enabled
completeness, non-empty aggregate evidence and actual complete assessor criteria

changed_from_reference.why: forced by measured throughput. A neutral pre-freeze load probe (no review content) measured 15.4 to 18.8 output tokens/s per stream at 12 concurrent streams (the schedule's peak: 3 cells x 4 reviewers) and 39 tokens/s alone. The reference sessions emitted median 892, p90 2,164, max 2,624 output tokens (Sol r2, 162 sessions); at 16 tokens/s a p90-sized session needs about 135 s of decode alone, so 120 s would time out sessions for throughput rather than protocol reasons. 600 s is the evaluator's own default --timeout-seconds and the LiteLLM gateway's request timeout; it covers the reference maximum (about 164 s at 16 tokens/s) with margin for this model's reasoning tokens. It was not tuned on any review output.
